root: For any feasible cut, balance at most four interface crossings per face gives a directed boundary-to-boundary path. Checkerboard face is balanced. Removing loops and using nonnegative capacities bounds the minimum. A simple corner crosscut conversely defines exact source-side separation. The n=2 case contains only forced edges.

Fixed path has 2N+b forward steps, reward k-b, and no positive cycle. Diagonal concatenation can be chosen simple or have nonpositive-reward cycles removed; thus expectation superadditive even without the cited L1 premise.

Each site uses a disjoint pair of outgoing marks. Monotone path through strict sites can consume either mark before the next anchor. Simplicity limits savings to one per site. I0 cancels in the upper bound; independent external marks serve only to enlarge this bound.

Use optimal-subpath monotone replacement for each two-real-anchor gap to get b_j<=ell_j. Final anchor is beyond all visited sites. Sum individual negative increments, and bound absolute part in the bad coordinate by twice backward variation. The time prefixes are disjoint.

Directly recover the factorized numerical W bound by multiplying exponential majorants for the gap predicate, the overshoot predicate and the anchored sum of h. The coordinate tilt is beta=2 gamma, geometric positive coordinate sums give the B0 factors; negative other increments use alpha-gamma sqrt(r). Indices count p=a-1+L. Large gamma then alpha then small r gives the needed convergence and uniform bound. The m=0 weight is purely numerical.

At fixed small q the exponentially small tail vanishes after division by volume. BGT finite-to-infinite strict-chain with planar constant 2 and r/(2q) to one produces sqrt(2q) only in stated order. Ordinary bond FPP has the wrong inequality for the desired upper bound.
